title: Internal Logical Induction for Pixel-Symbolic Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Reinforcement learning algorithms need to handle scenarios where pixel and symbolic inputs appear together, because the two input types provide complementary information.

gap.claim: Few reinforcement learning algorithms study problems involving mixed pixel and symbolic input types.

contributions.claim: An Internal Logical Induction framework integrates deep reinforcement learning and rule learning into one system.
The framework processes pixel input with deep reinforcement learning and induces propositional logic knowledge from symbolic input with rule learning.
The framework combines the two mechanisms by treating valuable induced knowledge as intrinsic rewards through reward shaping.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The Internal Logical Induction framework outperforms baseline approaches on reinforcement learning problems with pixel-symbolic input.
The framework's inductive knowledge has transferability advantages when pixel input semantics change.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reinforcement learning has advanced rapidly, but widely studied algorithms mainly focus on a single input form.
Pixel and symbolic inputs can occur together and offer complementary benefits, yet mixed-input reinforcement learning has received limited study.
The proposed framework combines deep reinforcement learning for pixel input, rule learning for symbolic input, and reward shaping based on valuable induced knowledge.
The authors report better performance than baseline approaches and transferability advantages when pixel input semantics change.
